rules.sourceText: Requirements for the Interdisciplinary Concentration in Africana Studies: Foundation Courses; Two courses from each of the following areas; Additional Requirements; Writing within the Discipline
Foundation Courses: AFS 101 - Themes in the Black Experience I; AFS 102 - Themes in the Black Experience II
Two courses from Africana Studies in the Humanities
Two courses from Africana Studies in the Social Sciences
Two courses from The African American Experience
Two courses from The Global African Experience

rules.text: Of the eight area courses, at least two must be selected from 200-level courses and at least five must be upper-division courses at the 300 or 400 level.

requirements.sourceText: Students select from an Interdisciplinary concentration, a concentration in Human Rights and Social Justice, and a concentration in Health and Disease. All courses for the major, except those graded S/U, must be passed with a letter grade of C or higher.

requirements.title: Total credits and upper-division credits

rule.text: Completion of the major requires 39 credits, including at least 21 upper-division credits (from courses numbered 300 or higher).
rule.reason: Program-wide credit totals are not a rule type the engine can evaluate.

requirements.title: Directed readings and independent study limit

rule.text: Only six credits of directed readings or independent study courses (courses numbered 447 and 487) may be used toward the major.
rule.reason: Program-wide credit cap across concentrations is not expressible as a single choose constraint.

requirements.title: Transfer student upper-division residency

rule.text: Transfer students must take at least 12 credits of upper-division Africana Studies courses in residence at Stony Brook to complete the AFS major.
rule.reason: Residency rule applies only to transfer students, which no policy type can condition on.

rule.text: Students must take at least two 200-level courses in Africana Studies prior to beginning their junior year.
rule.reason: Timing rule based on class standing is not expressible as a course rule.

policies.sourceText: All courses for the major, except those graded S/U, must be passed with a letter grade of C or higher.

notes.text: The concentration (Interdisciplinary, Human Rights & Social Justice, or Health & Disease) does not appear on the Stony Brook transcript; students should confirm their choice with an advisor.

Courses in the related-discipline slots of the sample sequence may not be crosslisted with AFH or AFS. Courses crosslisted with another department may be taken under either designator for credit, but not repeated under the other.

AFS 283, AFS 475, AFS 476, AFS 488, AFH 475, and AFH 476 may not be used to fulfill major requirements. AFS 283 may be taken for S/U credit (Community Service with the BlackWorld newspaper option) but does not count toward the major.
Students are recommended, but not required, to take AFS 491 - Interdisciplinary Seminar in Africana Studies.

Africana Studies Honors Program: departmental majors with a minimum G.P.A. of 3.33 in Africana Studies courses as specified in the major requirements and an overall G.P.A. of 3.0 may enroll at the beginning of their senior year. Not evaluated here.

Students may pursue minors of particular interest: Anthropology (ANT), Economics, BA (ECO), English (EGL), Health, Medicine, and Society (HMS), History (HIS), Philosophy (PHI), Political Science (POL).
